title: Microbundle pricing experiment: credit pools, rollover, and QSA readiness for rerank workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a controlled experiment for 'microbundle' vector credits that combine per-vector unit pricing with time-bound batch discounts and credit rollover. Target customers are heavy rerank users and search embeddings workloads. Goal: measure realized unit economics, customer acceptance of rollover credits, and operational complexity for contract/QSA workflows.
background: Customers frequently have bursty rerank traffic and dislike per-call variability in cost. Existing proposals (per-vector units, batch slots, bulk slabs) show tradeoffs between predictability and margin. This experiment tests a hybrid: small monthly bundles (microbundles) with built-in burst capacity, automatic rollover up to X%, and dynamic batch discounts that apply when system-level batching thresholds are hit.
acceptance_criteria: Calculated blended cost-per-vector for participating customers <= 0.9x current baseline for our Dedicated margin target
<5% incremental operational tickets caused by billing disputes during pilot
Sales/CS commit to offer microbundle in at least 10 enterprise negotiations during pilot window
QSA/legal sign-off language for rollover credits and pricing attachment completed
success_metrics: Unit economics: blended gross margin on participating accounts >= 60%
Revenue predictability: month-to-month variance in billable vectors reduced by >= 30% for enrolled customers
Adoption: pilot conversion rate (opt-in after trial) >= 25%
Support: fewer than 1 escalated billing incident per 50 pilot customers
approach: 1) Design microbundle SKUs: three sizes (S/M/L) mapping to low/medium/high monthly vector commitments. 2) Implement server-side metering rules: per-vector counter with monthly bucket and rollover cap (20%). 3) Apply batch discount engine to eligible requests when internal batching improves throughput; discount cascades apply after thresholds. 4) Create offer flow for sales (contract addendum + pricing attachment) and a QSA checklist for security/compliance review. 5) Run a 60-day pilot with 20 customers across Hosted and Dedicated environments.
technical_requirements: Billing metering updates: support monthly buckets with rollover cap
Console UI: product page showing microbundle balance, rollover amount, and projected overage
API changes: invoice_preview endpoint accepts microbundle SKU and returns estimated charge
Runtime telemetry: flag events when batch-discount thresholds were applied for a request
DB schema: lightweight table to track rollover state per customer (sharded by account id)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design): finalize SKUs and legal language (2 weeks). Phase 1 (Small pilot): enable 5 low-risk customers, monitor for 30 days (4 weeks). Phase 2 (Expanded pilot): onboard +15 customers across tiers and integrate with Sales offers (4 weeks). Phase 3 (Evaluation + QSA sign-off): collect metrics, update docs, decision gate to GA or iterate (2 weeks).
risks: Billing complexity may increase dispute volume if UI/UX is unclear
Metering edge cases for multi-region requests could miscount vectors leading to revenue leakage
Batch-discount elasticity: discount may cannibalize margin if customers shift patterns to exploit thresholds
Legal/QSA: rollover credits might create recognition/contractual accounting challenges
mitigations: Clear console and invoice line-items as first-class artifacts; include FAQs and examples
Add audit logs for per-request attribution and an admin reconciliation tool
Start with conservative discount multipliers and monitor with telemetry for behavior changes
Engage Finance and Legal early; include clear contract language limiting rollover percentage and expiry
open_questions: Exact rollover cap to offer for enterprise vs self-serve (10% vs 20%)?
How will refunds/credits be handled for accounts that terminate mid-cycle?
Should batch-discount be applied at request-time or as a post-hoc reconciliation line-item on invoice?
